solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Way-out Rhode Island red "thingy" primed for a big adventure!

indicators.note: primed means prepared or made ready, so these clue letters are worked up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An outlandish breed of chicken, a strange thingy, is all set for a grand trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The twenty-six letters of WAY-OUT RHODE ISLAND RED THINGY are rearranged, signalled by 'primed'. 'Way-out' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder. A Rhode Island Red is a breed of chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne's novel title names Phileas Fogg's celebrated globe-circling journey, a grand adventure.

clue.text: Rwanda right to get outside help to get off the ground

indicators.note: one piece gets outside the others, so it wraps round them as a container

parts.note: help means aid
RWA is the international country code for Rwanda

explanation.surface: Rwanda's right-wingers want foreign help to get a project started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get outside' wraps help round the other pieces, splitting it. 'to get off the ground' reads as an idiom for starting something, but the definition is literal: upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Airward means towards the air or skyward, which is moving up away from the ground.

clue.text: Well beaten at The Gabba?

parts.note: a team well beaten in a cricket match has been comprehensively bettered; read another way, a game at that Australian ground has been played out, start to finish

explanation.surface: Was a touring cricket side thrashed at the Brisbane ground?
explanation.walkthrough: The Gabba is the cricket ground in Brisbane, Australia. The question mark warns of the punning second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outplayed is to be beaten comprehensively by a superior opponent, as a team is when well beaten.

clue.text: Floating in the ocean at Antwerp

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something drifting on the sea near the Belgian port of Antwerp.
explanation.definitionFit: Natant is a formal or heraldic adjective meaning swimming or floating in water.

clue.text: Birds devastate Yemen's borders in first sweep

indicators.note: in places the border letters inside the word built from the rest

parts.note: to devastate is to wreck

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outermost letters, first and last
first takes just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A flock of birds lays waste to Yemen's frontier areas on its first pass.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of 'Yemen' are Y and N; they go inside WRECK followed by S (first of 'sweep'). 'Birds' is the plural subject, so read 'devastate' as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrynecks are small woodpecker-family birds named for their habit of twisting their necks.

clue.text: Part of Germany yields consistently rough ore

indicators.note: consistently here means at a regular, steady interval, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A German industrial region produces lumpy raw ore.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking every other letter of ROUGH ORE, starting with the first, gives R, U, H, R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr is a heavily industrial region of western Germany, famous for coal and steel.

clue.text: Indian city where it's said Elaine revealed all!

indicators.note: it's said signals that the words are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a woman called Elaine, or Ellie for short, who revealed all is a nude Ellie

explanation.surface: Rumour has a city where a woman called Elaine bared everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Ellie is a pet form of Elaine; 'nude Ellie' spoken sounds like the Indian capital's name.
explanation.definitionFit: New Delhi is the capital city of India.

clue.text: Touring car leaving Turin equipped for large load

indicators.note: leaving says the letters of the Italian city's name depart from the others
equipped means fitted out, so the remaining letters are set up afresh in a new order

parts.note: the city's letters are the ones removed

explanation.surface: A touring car is fitted out in Turin to carry a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of TURIN away from TOURING CAR and rearrange what is left, O G C A R. 'Touring' reads as describing the car but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the goods carried by a ship, aircraft or vehicle, a substantial load of freight.

clue.text: Musician from New Orleans makes maidens swoon?

indicators.note: to swoon is to faint and collapse, so the letters of the word fall into disorder

explanation.surface: A jazz player from New Orleans has young women fainting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link. New Orleans is the home of jazz, where a sideman is a band's supporting player.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideman is a supporting instrumentalist in a jazz or dance band, as opposed to the leader.

clue.text: Go round with Ethiopian opening pair, having a hill to climb

indicators.note: climbing goes upwards, against the direction of reading, so the whole assembly is read backwards
the opening pair are the word's first two letters

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An Ethiopian opening batting pair faces an uphill struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to climb' turns the whole run ET + A + TOR backwards. 'with' and 'having' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn about an axis, to go round and round.

clue.text: See 1
Back in Slovakia, limit team to a few cans of beer

indicators.note: in places the turned pieces inside the country code

parts.note: SK is the international code for Slovakia

indicators.note: back says the words that follow are written backwards

parts.note: to limit is to cap
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Back home in Slovakia, the coach limits the side to a little beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns CAP XI into IXPAC, which goes 'in' SK. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-pack is a set of six cans or bottles of beer sold together.

clue.text: Italian act (not first class) designed for deep water

indicators.note: not says the letters of the following item are to be left out of the pool
designed means planned or drawn up, so the letters left are arranged anew

parts.note: A1 means first class, its 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: An Italian performance, not the top-rated one, is staged for a sea setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and I (A1, first class) from ITALIAN ACT and rearrange the remaining T L A N T A C I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic is an ocean, and the ocean is deep water.

clue.text: London venue for team primarily requiring rehabilitation

indicators.note: primarily says the piece that comes after these words is needed first in the order

parts.note: reform is the act of rehabilitation, turning someone to better ways
a club is a sports team

explanation.surface: A London ground is chosen for a side that above all needs to be rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reform Club is a London gentlemen's club on Pall Mall, where Phileas Fogg makes his wager in the theme novel. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reform Club is a long-established gentlemen's club in Pall Mall, a London meeting place.

clue.text: Estonian city with an incredible pub

parts.note: a tall story is an incredible one
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: An Estonian town boasts a pub that is unbelievable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with an' are links; 'incredible' uses the sense of a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallinn is the capital of Estonia, on the Gulf of Finland.

clue.text: See 1
Landing in a wet part of Northern Ireland

parts.note: a wet, a splash of water, is a splash
Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A rainy arrival in a damp corner of Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A splashdown is a spacecraft's landing in the sea.

clue.text: Musical number for US resident

parts.note: Oklahoma! is the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical

explanation.surface: A show tune for an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical number' reads as a song from a show, but it splits into the musical plus N. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oklahoman lives in the US state of Oklahoma.

clue.text: Figure out price he charged after Damascus opening

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters following the single letter
the opening of a word is its first letter
charged in the sense of excited or agitated, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A man works out the price he was billed on arriving in Damascus.
explanation.walkthrough: D from 'Damascus opening' is followed by ECIPHER, an anagram of PRICE HE signalled by 'charged'.
explanation.definitionFit: To decipher is to work out or decode the meaning of something obscure.

clue.text: Secure site in outskirts of Porthcawl storing more film material

indicators.note: storing means holding something within, so the edges contain the other pieces
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: added means extra, more
cel is the transparent sheet used in animated film

explanation.surface: A secure building on the edge of a Welsh town stocks extra film supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Porthcawl is a Welsh seaside town; its outskirts are P and L, holding ADDED and CEL. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded cell is a cushioned room where a person is held safely, a secure place.

clue.text: Greek character overcoming fog and gales? No, it's our intrepid hero!

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcoming means sitting above, so the first piece comes before the rest

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: No signals that the words are not to be read as written but rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek battling fog and gales is hailed as the brave protagonist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcoming' puts the Greek letter on top in this down clue, and 'No' scrambles the weather words; 'it's' is a link. Phileas Fogg is the hero of the theme novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Phileas Fogg is Verne's bold protagonist who travels around the globe to win a bet.

clue.text: See 13
Mediterranean shrub bare, yet rampant

indicators.note: rampant means growing wildly and without restraint, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean bush is bare and yet growing out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay tree, or bay laurel, is an aromatic evergreen shrub native to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Game played with staff at Antarctic summit

parts.note: nim is a game of taking matchsticks or counters
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A game played with a stick on top of an Antarctic peak.
explanation.walkthrough: Mount Nimrod is in Antarctica, named after Shackleton's ship. 'played with' and 'at' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Nimrod is a peak in Antarctica's Transantarctic range, named for Shackleton's expedition ship.

clue.text: At home, Virginia is cool, but gets no benefit

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: Life in Virginia is fashionable but brings no rewards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'but gets' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in vain is done fruitlessly, with no benefit.

clue.text: French writer never needs to get involved

indicators.note: getting involved means becoming tangled up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written and rearranged; that the letters also run unbroken across 'never needs' is a coincidence of the setter's wording

explanation.surface: A French author refuses ever to get mixed up in things.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne was the French novelist who wrote the theme book.

clue.text: See 1
See 19
African animal — a pig on the ground

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the pig comes after the ground

parts.note: the earth is the ground
a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: An African beast is a pig lying on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The earth-hog is another name for the aardvark, a burrowing African mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: The earth-hog is an old name for the aardvark, a burrowing ant-eating mammal of Africa.

clue.text: Reading book with explosive device

definitions.meaning: a book for teaching children to read, an elementary textbook
a charge or cap used to set off an explosion

explanation.surface: A children's reader that comes with a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is both an elementary reading book and a detonator that ignites a charge.

clue.text: Cheap travel across the Pacific around Easter, for example

indicators.note: around signals that the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Budget passage over the Pacific taken around the Easter holiday, say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a time word placing the trip near the holiday, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest class of passenger accommodation on an ocean liner.

clue.text: Danish city where no-one is dimwitted

parts.note: no-one is nobody, nil, and the letter O looks like zero
dense means stupid, dimwitted

explanation.surface: A Danish town where nobody is stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Odense is Denmark's third-largest city, on the island of Funen.
